title: Giving a Heated Vest? Plan for the Battery, the Washing and the Fit
subtitle: A heated vest is only as warm as its battery, so here is what to buy with it, how long the heat lasts, and how to keep it working.
excerpt: Thinking of a heated vest for someone who is always cold? The vest is only half the gift. Here is how the battery, runtime, washing and sizing work, using one Gerbing vest as an example, based on the maker's own information.
author: Nickel And Gadget Editors

sections.content: A heated vest can be a thoughtful gift for someone who is always cold. It looks like a regular vest, but it has thin heating wires sewn inside and a small rechargeable battery that goes in a pocket.

What many gift-givers miss is that the vest is only half the story. How warm it feels, and for how long, depends on the battery. How long the vest lasts depends on how it is washed. This guide covers those parts. It is based on the maker's own product and care pages, not on independent reviews or our own testing, so treat the numbers as the maker's claims.

Inside the vest are heat zones, which are patches of fine wire that warm up when power flows through them. The Gerbing 7V Torrid Softshell Heated Vest 2.0 has four zones: two on the chest, one on the back and one at the neck.

The trade-off is simple: more heat means less time. Gerbing lists about 2 hours on a full charge at the highest setting, 3 hours at the next level down, 5 hours at the middle setting and 8 hours on the lowest. Cold weather and a low battery shorten those times.

The "7V" in the name tells you which battery system the vest uses. Heated clothing comes in separate systems. Gerbing's 7V batteries fit its 7V clothing, and its 12V batteries are for 12V gear. They are not interchangeable, so match the numbers when buying a spare.

items: Check what is in the box. On this vest, one 3400 mAh battery and a wall charger are included, and a spare battery costs extra.
Check the runtime at a comfortable setting, not just the longest number on the page.
Read the care instructions before buying. Some heated gear is machine washable with the battery removed; other items are hand-wash only.
Check the size chart. This vest is a men's fit, offered in sizes S to XXL.
Know the return window and warranty in case the size is wrong or something stops working.
Add shipping to the total. Gerbing calculates it at checkout.
Ask the wearer's doctor or pharmacist if you are unsure whether heated clothing is a good idea for them.

sections.content: Setting it up and caring for it

If you are giving the vest as a gift, consider charging the battery before you wrap it. Gerbing says to charge fully before first use, which takes about three hours. When the vest is put away between outings, Gerbing advises keeping the battery at least 25 percent charged.

A good first step is to start on the lowest setting and turn it up only if needed. Gerbing's page lists up to 135°F as the maximum heat. That is the top setting of the device, not a safe temperature for skin contact.

Washing is where heated clothing is most often damaged. Gerbing says most of its 7V garments can go in the machine on a gentle, cold cycle, but only after the battery is taken out. Afterward, let the vest air dry completely. Do not put it in the dryer, iron it or use a heat gun on it.
"Never machine wash batteries, chargers, or accessories." (Gerbing Battery & Garment Care page)

Heat can cause burns without a warning sensation, especially if someone has reduced feeling in their skin. Please talk with the wearer's doctor before giving heated clothing, and follow the maker's instructions. If you have a medical concern about a burn or injury, contact a doctor, and in an emergency call 911.
sections.label: Before You Buy

sections.content: A heated vest can be a cozy gift for a chilly friend or parent. Charge it before you wrap it, and remind them to take the battery out before washing. That small bit of planning helps the warmth last.
